name: SonicBridge
subtitle: Private TV Audio. Reimagined.
description: An Android-powered low-latency audio streaming system that transforms a TV into a personal wireless listening experience. SonicBridge captures TV audio and streams high-quality stereo sound over the local Wi-Fi network to Android devices—without expensive hardware or internet connectivity.
problem: Watching television late at night often means lowering the volume or disturbing everyone else. Bluetooth introduces latency, wired headphones reduce comfort, and premium wireless systems are expensive.
focus: SonicBridge explores how software engineering can solve this problem using devices people already own.

approach.name: Capture
approach.detail: Read TV playback audio through the Android Audio Playback Capture API.

approach.name: Transport
approach.detail: Use the local Wi-Fi network to avoid Bluetooth latency and internet dependency.

approach.name: Playback
approach.detail: Decode stereo PCM on an Android phone through a foreground service.

approach.name: Validate
approach.detail: Tune buffers, lifecycle behavior, and reconnection paths for a dependable listening experience.

why: Local Wi-Fi provides the bandwidth and control needed for low-latency stereo audio, while keeping the system offline, affordable, and within devices people already own.
related: Shockwave focuses on immersive room audio. SonicBridge focuses on private personal audio. Both are part of the same mission: engineering affordable entertainment experiences through intelligent software and system design.
